industry.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence moved towards the tape. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): third-quarter beats were sold (Sandvik down 5%, Atlas Copco down 8%, Hiab down 12%), Danske Bank's C-J (25 October) says 'a lot is priced in' with the order strength coming from data centres the market no longer pays for, and the exception is the non-AI compounder (Hexagon, 13% organic growth); against it, offshore services and nuclear have multi-year visibility and electrical equipment is still the physical bottleneck. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, C prior. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment, Diversified groups, Distributors, Test and measurement and Engineered components at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Five live holdings (19.35 points of the book) sit here, judged in component 4. Counter-case for D: a tape that sells beats is a regime statement; for B: the order data remain the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack. To D on a second week of beats sold with relative strength falling to F.

sector.key: O.4. Electrical equipment, grid and automation
sector.why: Neutral, carried, with both sides stronger again. The demand: Jefferies' power analyst (28 October) raised the 2027 US data-centre build to about 27 gigawatts from the low twenties on satellite imaging, Fortum's 22-year nuclear agreement and rising Nordic power forwards say the grid is the constraint. The tape: ABB fell 6% on 40% order growth because the strength was data centres and the market 'is not willing at all to pay up for beats related to DC and AI' (Danske Bank, 25 October); Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, C prior, improved from last week's F reading. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): grid programmes are debt-funded with the ten-year above 5%. Two live holdings, Alfen (4.60%) and Arteche (3.28%), judged in component 4. Counter-case for D: the market's refusal to pay for data-centre orders is new since the summer and may last; for B: the binding constraint on the largest capital-spending theme is this sector's product. Moves to B if relative strength returns to B with the AI-infrastructure proxies recovering; to D on an F reading with hyperscaler capital spending guides cut.

geography.why: Double Underweight, carried. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the French ten-year premium reached a record 150 basis points, 'a lot for a core European country' (Pacific, 26 October), the 2027 deficit is seen at 5.4% of output (Goldman Sachs, 25 October), euro-exposed assets underperformed their global betas because of France (GOAL, 26 October), 2027's 300 billion of issuance makes this 'just the warmup' and the election in May or June 2027 is the earliest point anything changes; against it, Moody's affirmation removed a sovereign tail risk (DNB Carnegie, 26 October) and the French Hidden Champions newsletter sees institutional outflows from French small and mid caps as a contrarian set-up. Ten Pool names, TotalEnergies at rank 24 near the Bench cut with a global revenue base the row does not describe well. Counter-case: the affirmation and the contrarian set-up. To D on the premium under 120 basis points for a month; back to C under 100.
